about: The reading meter's prices: one table that both the meter in the reader's browser (api/v1/billing/meter.json, made by newsroom/build/features/billing.mjs) and the published billing page (/account/billing.html) are generated from, so the page and the meter cannot disagree. The model is the one php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai runs (its data/billing.json, read 5 November 2026) and newsroom.sgit.ai's meter (sg-meter v1.5.0): a base price per kind of page, a multiplier for how fresh the page is, times the share of it read, never under a tenth. Edited by hand; the gate checks it against its schema and the feature's own rules.
formula: price = max(floor, round(base[type] x freshness[tier])), then x the share of the page read (never under a tenth) x the reader's usefulness rating (1 free, 3 the price, 5 double)

reference_types.why: A conclusion someone signed, written against a stated state of the evidence: the most judgement per word on the site.
The most compressed form of the work: one page for one reader's decision.
Work a reader cannot do by reading one source: counting, comparing, converting times.
Pages assembled by agents; the reader pays for the assembly.
Reference pages: the value is in checking, and checking must never cost more at the moment it matters most.
The site's account of itself: metered at the floor, never more.
The meter's own pages. Charging a reader to see their bill is not a price.

types.why: A signed article is PrompTugal.news's own judgement, with its limits and sources: the reference's article, unchanged.
A profile is assembled from several sources, re-checked at the source, with the company's sessions, people and related companies: work a reader cannot do from one page.
Every company in a field, counted and compared, with the field's sessions: the same kind of work as a profile.
Assembled from the curator's captures by agents: the reference's story.
One programme item with its speakers, place and source, assembled from the programme by agents; it decays because it matters most in the days around it.

tiers.why: The first day: when the content is news and a reader is deciding something now.
The first week: still the current state of a developing story.
The base price: settled enough to rely on, recent enough to act on.
The record: worth reading, priced for the reader doing history, never free.

age_from: The page's own date (<meta name="page-date">): for an article the day it was written, for a page made from data the day its source last changed. The age is worked out in the reader's browser, so the same release serves the same table to everyone.
rules: Every content page is metered. The only unmetered pages are the meter's own: your account, top up, topped up and your vault.
The price depends on two things only: what kind of page it is, and how fresh it is. Not on who is reading, not on demand, not on the topic.
Fresh costs more and the price halves into the archive, never to zero. Reference pages and the site's account of itself do not decay and stay at the floor.
A page costs its price times the share of it you read, never less than a tenth; once per page per browser session; rating it re-prices it from free to double.
Nothing is ever blocked. The balance can go below zero, and a reader can decline to pay for a page and say why.
Everything is kept in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose: a top-up (on Stripe's own page) or your vault.
This table is published here and the meter is generated from the same data file, so the page and the meter cannot disagree.
